title: Dark depth-tinted water with multi-octave normal chop
note: Water carries a dark depth-tinted base and real roughness; a pale mirror-grey plane is an automatic fail.
intent: Judged against a reference, a pale mirror-grey water plane is the single most repeated rejection: the water histogram must not peak above mid-grey, and the plane must sit at least 2 stops darker than the sky and darker than the stone banks. Give it an explicit dark depth-tinted base — shallow #2b3324 olive-grey to deep #141a10 (or #4a5540 → #232a1c), roughness ≈ 0.35, reflectivity ≤ 0.3 — with toneMappingExposure 0.6–0.8 so stone and moss stay saturated. Chop is a normal perturbation, never geometry bands: sum ≥ 3 noise octaves whose wavelengths span at least 8:1 (e.g. 4 m / 1 m / 0.25 m, with the fine band in 0.15–0.4 m) at different speeds, because a single wavelength, or a plane displaced on a grid coarser than 0.2 units, reads as "hard banded ripple".

check.js: materials('water').length > 0 && materials('water').every(m => { const c = m.color || (m.uniforms && m.uniforms.uBase && m.uniforms.uBase.value); return !!c && c.getHSL({ h: 0, s: 0, l: 0 }, 'srgb').l <= 0.22 && (m.roughness === undefined || m.roughness >= 0.3); })
check.note: Tagged water carries a dark depth-tinted base (sRGB lightness <= 0.22, e.g. #2b3324) and roughness >= 0.3; a pale mirror-grey plane is an automatic fail.

port: Replace the facet’s water material (src/water.js or the terrain-water module) with this base and tag the mesh "water"; if the mirror recipe’s ShaderMaterial is used instead, keep its uBase uniform at the same dark hex so the check reads it. Verify from the default camera that the water is darker in value than both sky and banks before touching chop or reflection strength.

evidence.note: Seyda Neen runs, 5+ rejections: never a pale mirror-grey plane; color 0x2b3324, roughness 0.35, exposure 0.6–0.8; chop ≥3 octaves, no grid coarser than 0.2 units
explicit dark base #2b3323 with depth tinting, reflectivity ≤0.3, water darker than sky and stone banks; histogram must not peak above mid-grey
pin shallow/deep hex (#4a5540 → #232a1c), reflectivity as a 0–1 number, chop wavelength 0.15–0.4 m
#2b3320 shallow to #141a10 deep, ≥2 stops darker than sky; chop ≥3 octaves spanning ≥8:1 (4 m / 1 m / 0.25 m)
